message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# .github/workflows/run-tests.yaml
name: test
on: [ push, pull_request ]
concurrency:
  group: "${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}"
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  run-tests:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        implementation:
          - sbcl
          - ecl
          - ccl
        include:
          - implementation: sbcl
            image: clfoundation/sbcl:2.2.4
            command: sbcl
          - implementation: ecl
            image: clfoundation/ecl:21.2.1
            command: ecl
          - implementation: ccl
            image: clfoundation/ccl:1.12
            command: ccl
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: ${{ matrix.image }}
      env:
        CI_SYSTEM: github
        QUICKLISP_ADD_TO_INIT_FILE: true
        QUICKLISP_DIST_VERSION: latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Run tests
        run: |
          env LISP=${{ matrix.command }} ./scripts/run-ci-tests.sh",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs on push and pull_request with a matrix of three Lisp implementations. The P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE pattern (cancel superseded runs) is supported by evidence showing superseding runs can reduce duplicate work. Adding a workflow-level concurrency group keyed by workflow and ref with cancel-in-progress:true cancels stale in-progress runs when a newer revision lands on the same branch/PR, while each completed run still executes the full matrix and test command, preserving build and test coverage. Contraindications do not apply: this is a test workflow rather than release/deployment work, and the group includes github.ref so distinct branches and PRs are isolated. No permissions are weakened and no privileged actions, secrets, publishing/deployment operations, or new network access are added.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE", "experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-560f8aa17cf2dbe5"]
}
